service.name: Corporate holiday party entertainment in Denver
service.serviceType: Live music and DJ for corporate holiday parties
service.description: Live music for Denver corporate holiday parties, duo through quartet plus DJ, across the season's 21 November and December dates.

faqs.q: What does a corporate holiday party band cost in Denver?
faqs.a: A cover or jazz band for a corporate event runs {{market:us_corporate_band}} in this market, and a Denver holiday weekend carries {{market:denver_holiday_surcharge}} on top across the market. Those are the market's figures. Signet does not publish prices: send the date, the venue and the guest count, and you get our number for that night.

faqs.q: How many holiday party dates does Denver actually have?
faqs.a: Twenty-one. Thursdays, Fridays and Saturdays across November and December 2026, minus Thanksgiving and Christmas, come to 21 party dates, and 10 of them are in December. They are laid out on this page. Whether one is free is a booking-calendar question: send the date and the venue by email.

faqs.q: What does load-in look like at a downtown Denver hotel?
faqs.a: Through the dock and the service elevator, inside the windows the venue sets. We coordinate dock time, elevator window and power with the venue before the day. A band needs 45 to 90 minutes to load in depending on size, plus one or two dedicated 20-amp circuits; the full sheet by size is on our technical page.

faqs.q: Do December dates in Denver cost more?
faqs.a: The strong December dates do, here and everywhere in this market: a holiday weekend in Denver carries {{market:denver_holiday_surcharge}}. New Year's Eve is its own case again. What that means for your date is named before you sign rather than after, and it is never folded into a headline figure.

faqs.q: When should a Denver company book its holiday party?
faqs.a: August through October. That is when the season is decided for November and December dates, and New Year's Eve books earliest of all. Booking early buys the date rather than a lower number, which on a December Saturday is the thing actually worth having.
